newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: LATAM STOCKS SEEN UNSETTLED IN WEEK, WARY OF FED.
newsitem.headline: LATAM STOCKS SEEN UNSETTLED IN WEEK, WARY OF FED.

text.p: Latin America's main bourses were expected to behave erratically this week as jitters mount ahead of the U.S. Federal Reserve talks August 19, dealers said.
"This week's looming U.S. inflation data, which should give us a pretty good idea of the Fed's auction, will keep the markets in check," said Nestor de Cessare at Argentine traders Allaria Ledesma.
In Brazil, stocks were seen hurt also by weaker cash flows blamed on the market's futures and options expirations next Wednesday and Monday, respectively.

Traders noted foreign investors usually keep a low profile before the settlements, when the market is driven by speculators. "I don't think foreigners like to trade in this environment," said John Carioba of brokers Indusval.
Last week, Brazil's Bovespa index fell 1.0 percent, closing at 12,128 points and stretching losses so far in August to 5.7 percent. Stocks have still surged more than 70 percent this year.
In Mexico, analysts said they expected the bolsa to take its cue from the U.S. markets, awaiting U.S. retail sales due Wednesday, followed by consumer prices on Thursday.
But stocks were seen underpinned by strong local fundamentals.
"The bourse is indeed susceptible to the Dow, but internal factors weigh more and those factors are very positive," said Alexander Anderson, research head at the Abaco brokerage.

Analysts said despite the volatile patch in New York ahead of the Fed talks, foreign investment flows to Mexico that fuelled a recent rally to record levels could resume as share valuations were still relatively attractive. They noted stocks were still far below all-time highs in dollar terms.

The IPC index ended at 5,075.05 Friday, up 8.02 points or 0.2 percent on the week after profit-taking and overspill from U.S. markets wiped out strong earlier gains. Argentine traders expected the Buenos Aires market to drift sideways and stay focused on U.S. long bond yields.
"The underlying tone here is firm. But this week we want to know what the Fed will do, and the way long bond yields behave can be a good indicator of this," one dealer said.
The blue-chip MerVal index pushed 1.2 percent higher last week to end at 850.73 Friday.
In Chile, stocks were expected to resume their downward tilt as the market regroups following the second-quarter reporting season which ended a week ago.
"We'll probably see more of the same this week as there was a nice run-up on the back of second quarter earnings," said David Hurd, head of research at Merrill Lynch in Santiago.
Players took profits recently following gains sparked by stronger-than-expected earnings from many companies, with the 40-share .IPSA index shedding 1.2 percent to 134.08 points.
The market is expected to remain flat in August as a result of the U.S. summer holidays and as local investors wait for another central bank interest rate cut, traders said.

Venezuelan stocks were seen soft on lingering tension between union and business leaders over wage rises, even though they staged a brief recovery after the first national strike in eight years last Wednesday.
The 12-hour stoppage ended without violence and calmed the market, which rebounded for two sessions.
But investors remained cautious.
The market's 19-share index ended the week with a loss of 1.0 percent at 9,344.05.
((-- Buenos Aires Newsroom 541 318-0657))
